     5	/-!
     6	# Seed-fiber dilation for the directly indexed low-degree game
     7	
     8	This module dilates a seed-indexed low-degree strategy by a maximally
     9	correlated residue register.  Block-diagonal projective measurements retain
    10	arbitrary dependence on the seed within each `chiIndex` fiber.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-458`
    15	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
    16	-/
    17	
    18	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    23	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    24	
    25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	/-! ## Projective block measurements -/
    28	
    29	/-- Relabel a matrix measurement along an equivalence of outcome alphabets. -/
    30	noncomputable def matrixMeasurementTransport
    31	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    32	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    33	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota) :
    34	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement beta iota :=
    35	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    36	    (fun b => M.effect (e.symm b))
    37	    (fun b => M.pos (e.symm b))
    38	    (by
    39	      calc
    40	        ∑ b, M.effect (e.symm b) = ∑ a, M.effect a :=
    41	          Equiv.sum_comp e.symm M.effect
    42	        _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one)
    43	
    44	@[simp] theorem matrixMeasurementTransport_effect
    45	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    46	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    47	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    48	    (b : beta) :
    49	    (matrixMeasurementTransport e M).effect b = M.effect (e.symm b) :=
    50	  rfl
    51	
    52	/-- Relabeling a projective matrix measurement preserves projectivity. -/
    53	theorem matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
    54	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    55	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    56	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    57	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) :
    58	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (matrixMeasurementTransport e M) :=
    59	  fun b => hM (e.symm b)
    60	
    61	/-- Assemble a family of matrix measurements as diagonal blocks indexed by a
    62	finite classical register. -/
    63	noncomputable def blockDiagonalMeasurement
    64	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
    65	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    66	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block]
    67	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota) :
    68	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block) :=
    69	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    70	    (fun a => Matrix.blockDiagonal fun r => (M r).effect a)
    71	    (fun a => Matrix.blockDiagonal_nonneg
    72	      (fun r => (M r).effect a) (fun r => (M r).pos a))
    73	    (by
    74	      ext ⟨i, r⟩ ⟨j, s⟩
    75	      simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply]
    76	      by_cases hrs : r = s
    77	      · subst s
    78	        simp only [if_pos]
    79	        calc
    80	          ∑ x, (M r).effect x i j = (1 : Matrix iota iota ℂ) i j :=
    81	            by
    82	              simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using
    83	                congrFun (congrFun (M r).sum_eq_one i) j
    84	          _ = (1 : Matrix (iota × block) (iota × block) ℂ)
    85	              (i, r) (j, r) := by
    86	                change (if i = j then 1 else 0) =
    87	                  (if (i, r) = (j, r) then 1 else 0)
    88	                simp
    89	      · simp [hrs])
    90	
    91	@[simp] theorem blockDiagonalMeasurement_effect
    92	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
    93	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    94	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block]
    95	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    96	    (a : alpha) :
    97	    (blockDiagonalMeasurement M).effect a =
    98	      Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a) :=
    99	  rfl
   100	
   101	/-- A block-diagonal family of projective measurements is projective. -/
   102	theorem blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   103	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
   104	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   105	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block]
   106	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
   107	    (hM : ∀ r, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (M r)) :
   108	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (blockDiagonalMeasurement M) := by
   109	  intro a
   110	  constructor
   111	  · change Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a) *
   112	        Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a) =
   113	      Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a)
   114	    rw [← Matrix.blockDiagonal_mul]
   115	    congr 1
   116	    funext r
   117	    exact (hM r a).isIdempotentElem.eq
   118	  · change (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a))ᴴ =
   119	      Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a)
   120	    rw [Matrix.blockDiagonal_conjTranspose]
   121	    congr 1
   122	    funext r
   123	    exact (hM r a).isSelfAdjoint.star_eq
   124	
   125	/-! ## The correlated residue state -/
   126	
   127	/-- The normalized maximally correlated state on the common seed-fiber
   128	residue. -/
   129	noncomputable def seedResidueAncilla (L : LdParams) :
   130	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
   131	      (Fin (L.q / L.m) × Fin (L.q / L.m)) := by
   132	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   133	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   134	  exact eprState (Fin (L.q / L.m))
   135	
   136	/-- The seed-residue ancilla has unit norm. -/
   137	theorem seedResidueAncilla_norm (L : LdParams) :
   138	    ‖seedResidueAncilla L‖ = 1 := by
   139	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   140	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   141	  exact eprState_norm (Fin (L.q / L.m))
   142	
   143	/-- Reindexing Euclidean coordinates along an equivalence preserves norm. -/
   144	theorem reindexState_norm_eq
   145	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   146	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   147	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   148	    (e : iota ≃ kappa) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
   149	    ‖reindexState e psi‖ = ‖psi‖ := by
   150	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)]
   151	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
   152	  change (∑ j : kappa, ‖psi (e.symm j)‖ ^ 2) = ∑ i : iota, ‖psi i‖ ^ 2
   153	  exact e.symm.sum_comp (fun i => ‖psi i‖ ^ 2)
   154	
   155	/-- The coordinate tensor of two Euclidean vectors has the product norm. -/
   156	theorem vecTensor_norm_eq
   157	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   158	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   159	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   160	    (u : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ kappa) :
   161	    ‖vecTensor u v‖ = ‖u‖ * ‖v‖ := by
   162	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _))]
   163	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, mul_pow, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq,
   164	    EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
   165	  change (∑ p : iota × kappa, ‖u p.1 * v p.2‖ ^ 2) =
   166	    (∑ i : iota, ‖u i‖ ^ 2) * ∑ j : kappa, ‖v j‖ ^ 2
   167	  simp only [norm_mul, mul_pow]
   168	  rw [← Finset.univ_product_univ, Finset.sum_product, Finset.sum_mul]
   169	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   170	  intro i hi
   171	  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   172	
   173	/-- Tensor the original strategy state with the maximally correlated residue
   174	state and shuffle the factors back into the two local carriers. -/
   175	noncomputable def seedFiberLiftedState
   176	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams) :
   177	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
   178	      ((S.ιA × Fin (L.q / L.m)) × (S.ιB × Fin (L.q / L.m))) :=
   179	  reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor S.ψ (seedResidueAncilla L))
   180	
   181	/-- The correlated seed-fiber lift preserves normalization of the strategy
   182	state. -/
   183	theorem seedFiberLiftedState_norm
   184	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams) :
   185	    ‖seedFiberLiftedState S L‖ = 1 := by
   186	  rw [seedFiberLiftedState, reindexState_norm_eq, vecTensor_norm_eq,
   187	    S.ψ_norm, seedResidueAncilla_norm, one_mul]
   188	
   189	/-! ## From the seed-indexed game to the direct game -/
   190	
   191	/-- The seed-indexed question selected in one residue block of a direct
   192	question.  Applying `ldCL` ensures that irrelevant ambient coordinates are
   193	canonicalized exactly as in the source game. -/
   194	noncomputable def seededLdQuestion (L : LdParams)
   195	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   196	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) : LdQuestion L :=
   197	  (q.1, ldCL L q.1 (ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L q.2 residue))
   198	
   199	/-- Dilate a strategy for the seed-indexed low-degree game to the directly
   200	indexed game.  The two local carriers receive correlated copies of the seed
   201	residue, and each measurement is block diagonal in that residue. -/
   202	noncomputable def ldStrategyToDirect (L : LdParams)
   203	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L)) : Strategy (directLdGame L.toDirectLdParams) where
   204	  ιA := S.ιA × Fin (L.q / L.m)
   205	  ιB := S.ιB × Fin (L.q / L.m)
   206	  ψ := seedFiberLiftedState S L
   207	  ψ_norm := seedFiberLiftedState_norm S L
   208	  A q := blockDiagonalMeasurement fun residue =>
   209	    matrixMeasurementTransport (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L)
   210	      (S.A (seededLdQuestion L q residue))
   211	  B q := blockDiagonalMeasurement fun residue =>
   212	    matrixMeasurementTransport (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L)
   213	      (S.B (seededLdQuestion L q residue))
   214	
   215	/-- Projectivity is preserved by the correlated seed-fiber dilation. -/
   216	theorem ldStrategyToDirect_isProjective (L : LdParams)
   217	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L)) (hS : S.IsProjective) :
   218	    (ldStrategyToDirect L S).IsProjective := by
   219	  constructor
   220	  · intro q
   221	    apply blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   222	    intro residue
   223	    apply matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
   224	    exact hS.1 (seededLdQuestion L q residue)
   225	  · intro q
   226	    apply blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   227	    intro residue
   228	    apply matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
   229	    exact hS.2 (seededLdQuestion L q residue)
   230	
   231	@[simp] theorem ldStrategyToDirect_A_effect (L : LdParams)
   232	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L))
   233	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   234	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer L.toDirectLdParams) :
   235	    ((ldStrategyToDirect L S).A q).effect answer =
   236	      Matrix.blockDiagonal fun residue =>
   237	        (S.A (seededLdQuestion L q residue)).effect
   238	          ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm answer) :=
   239	  rfl
   240	
   241	@[simp] theorem ldStrategyToDirect_B_effect (L : LdParams)
   242	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L))
   243	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   244	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer L.toDirectLdParams) :
   245	    ((ldStrategyToDirect L S).B q).effect answer =
   246	      Matrix.blockDiagonal fun residue =>
   247	        (S.B (seededLdQuestion L q residue)).effect
   248	          ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm answer) :=
   249	  rfl
   250	
   251	/-- A direct question reconstructed in a residue block parses back to its
   252	canonical direct form. -/
   253	theorem parse_seededLdQuestion (L : LdParams)
   254	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   255	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   256	    parseLdQuestion L (seededLdQuestion L q residue) =
   257	      (q.1, directLdMap L.toDirectLdParams q.1 q.2) := by
   258	  exact parseLdQuestion_ldCL_ofDirectResidue L q.1 q.2 residue
   259	
   260	/-- Coordinate formula for the correlated residue lift. -/
   261	theorem seedFiberLiftedState_apply
   262	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams)
   263	    (i : S.ιA) (j : S.ιB)
   264	    (r s : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   265	    seedFiberLiftedState S L ((i, r), (j, s)) =
   266	      if r = s then
   267	        S.ψ (i, j) * (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card (Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹
   268	      else 0 := by
   269	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   270	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   271	  simp [seedFiberLiftedState, reindexState, vecTensor, seedResidueAncilla,
   272	    eprState, prodShuffle]
   273	
   274	end
   275	
   276	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# The directly indexed low-degree game
     6	
     7	This module defines polynomial evaluation, questions, answers, and the game
     8	for the directly indexed low-degree interface.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The underlying game is `def:ld-game` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with source origin
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    23	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    24	
    25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	/-- Coefficient lists for a univariate polynomial of degree at most `c` in the
    28	direct scalar field. -/
    29	abbrev DirectDegPoly (D : DirectLdParams) (c : ℕ) :=
    30	  Fin (c + 1) → DirectScalarQ D
    31	
    32	/-- A direct line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` lies on the line
    33	and every parameter presenting `u` gives value `a`.  The universal clause
    34	keeps the zero-direction case explicit. -/
    35	def DirectEvaluatesTo {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : DirectLineDesc D)
    36	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    37	    (a : DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
    38	  (∃ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
    39	    ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction →
    40	      evalCoefficient f t = a
    41	
    42	/-- Option-completed evaluation of a direct line polynomial.  `none` is an
    43	explicit outcome when the point does not determine an evaluation; no field
    44	value is used as a fallback. -/
    45	noncomputable def directEvalOpt {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ}
    46	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    47	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) : Option (DirectScalarQ D) := by
    48	  classical
    49	  exact if h : ∃ a : DirectScalarQ D, DirectEvaluatesTo line f u a then
    50	    some (Classical.choose h)
    51	  else none
    52	
    53	/-- The typed question alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    54	abbrev DirectLdQuestion (D : DirectLdParams) := LdType × DirectLdSpace D
    55	
    56	/-- Canonicalize a common direct sample for one question type.  Irrelevant
    57	coordinates are fixed, so point questions reveal no sampled line index and
    58	axis-line questions reveal no diagonal direction. -/
    59	noncomputable def directLdMap (D : DirectLdParams) :
    60	    LdType → DirectLdSpace D → DirectLdSpace D
    61	  | .point, sample => ⟨sample.point, D.firstIndex, 0⟩
    62	  | .aline, sample =>
    63	      let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
    64	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, 0⟩
    65	  | .dline, sample =>
    66	      let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
    67	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, direction⟩
    68	
    69	/-- The directly indexed question distribution.  It has the same uniform
    70	ordered type-pair branches as `ldQuestionDistribution`, but its common sample
    71	contains an actual coordinate index rather than a field seed. -/
    72	noncomputable def directLdQuestionDistribution (D : DirectLdParams) :
    73	    Distribution (DirectLdQuestion D × DirectLdQuestion D) :=
    74	  (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
    75	    ((sample.1.1, directLdMap D sample.1.1 sample.2),
    76	      (sample.1.2, directLdMap D sample.1.2 sample.2))
    77	
    78	/-- The directly indexed question law is probabilistic. -/
    79	theorem directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
    80	    (directLdQuestionDistribution D).IsProbability := by
    81	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability
    82	    ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map _
    83	
    84	/-- The answer alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    85	inductive DirectLdAnswer (D : DirectLdParams) where
    86	  | pointVals (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)
    87	  | alinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    88	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    89	  deriving DecidableEq
    90	
    91	/-- A finite code for the directly indexed answer alphabet. -/
    92	abbrev DirectLdAnswerCode (D : DirectLdParams) :=
    93	  (Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    94	    ((Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    95	      (Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D))
    96	
    97	/-- Constructor-preserving equivalence between the inductive answer type and
    98	its finite code. -/
    99	noncomputable def directLdAnswerEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   100	    DirectLdAnswer D ≃ DirectLdAnswerCode D where
   101	  toFun
   102	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   103	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   104	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   105	  invFun
   106	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   107	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   108	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   109	  left_inv := by intro answer; cases answer <;> rfl
   110	  right_inv := by
   111	    intro answer
   112	    rcases answer with a | a
   113	    · rfl
   114	    · rcases a with a | a <;> rfl
   115	
   116	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Inhabited (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   117	  ⟨.pointVals 0⟩
   118	
   119	noncomputable instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Fintype (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   120	  Fintype.ofEquiv (DirectLdAnswerCode D) (directLdAnswerEquiv D).symm
   121	
   122	/-- Check that a direct-game answer has the constructor required by its
   123	question type. -/
   124	def validDirectLdAnswer {D : DirectLdParams} (t : LdType)
   125	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) : Bool :=
   126	  match t, answer with
   127	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   128	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   129	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   130	  | _, _ => false
   131	
   132	/-- The directly indexed axis-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   133	def directAlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   134	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   135	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   136	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   137	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   138	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection line.index →
   139	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   140	
   141	/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   142	def directDlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   143	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   144	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   145	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   146	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   147	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   148	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   149	
   150	/-- The directly indexed low-degree win predicate.  It differs from
   151	`ldWinPredicate` only by reading the coordinate index directly from each line
   152	question. -/
   153	noncomputable def directLdWinPredicate (D : DirectLdParams) :
   154	    DirectLdQuestion D → DirectLdQuestion D →
   155	      DirectLdAnswer D → DirectLdAnswer D → Bool :=
   156	  open Classical in
   157	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   158	    if validDirectLdAnswer tA a && validDirectLdAnswer tB b then
   159	      match tA, tB, a, b with
   160	      | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   161	      | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   162	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   163	      | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   164	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   165	      | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   166	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   167	      | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   168	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   169	      | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   170	      | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   171	      | _, _, _, _ => true
   172	    else false
   173	
   174	/-- The directly indexed low-degree game at an arbitrary positive dimension.
   175	It is an internal analysis game, not the conditionally linear verifier game
   176	`ldGame`. -/
   177	noncomputable def directLdGame (D : DirectLdParams) : Game where
   178	  QuestionA := DirectLdQuestion D
   179	  QuestionB := DirectLdQuestion D
   180	  AnswerA := DirectLdAnswer D
   181	  AnswerB := DirectLdAnswer D
   182	  μ := directLdQuestionDistribution D
   183	  μ_prob := directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability D
   184	  decide := directLdWinPredicate D
   185	
   186	/-- The canonical point question associated with a geometric point. -/
   187	def directLdPointQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   188	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   189	  (.point, ⟨u, D.firstIndex, 0⟩)
   190	
   191	/-- Total point-answer relabeling used in the direct soundness conclusion.
   192	Wrong-form answers are folded into the zero tuple, exactly as for
   193	`ldPointValuesOrZero`. -/
   194	def directLdPointValuesOrZero (D : DirectLdParams) :
   195	    DirectLdAnswer D → Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D
   196	  | .pointVals values => values
   197	  | .alinePolys _ => 0
   198	  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   199	
   200	/-- A simultaneous tuple of bounded polynomials for the directly indexed
   201	game. -/
   202	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyTuple (D : DirectLdParams) :=
   203	  Fin D.k → PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d
   204	
   205	/-- A polynomial-tuple POVM for the directly indexed game. -/
   206	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyMeasTuple (D : DirectLdParams) (ι : Type*)
   207	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   208	  Measurement (DirectPolyTuple D) ι
   209	
   210	/-- Evaluate every component of a direct polynomial tuple at a point. -/
   211	def evalDirectPolyTupleAt {D : DirectLdParams}
   212	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (g : DirectPolyTuple D) :
   213	    Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D :=
   214	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   215	
   216	end
   217	
   218	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.Defs
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Section 3 — Strategy core
     5	
     6	Base state-invariance and strategy structures for the low individual degree test.
     7	-/
     8	
     9	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    10	
    11	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT
    12	
    13	instance : Fintype Role where
    14	  elems := {Role.A, Role.B}
    15	  complete r := by
    16	    cases r <;> simp
    17	
    18	/-- The SWAP reindexing on `ι × ι`: permutes the two tensor factors.
    19	`swapDensity M (i₁,i₂) (j₁,j₂) = M (i₂,i₁) (j₂,j₁)`. -/
    20	def swapDensity {ι : Type*} (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    21	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι) :=
    22	  Matrix.of fun (ij : ι × ι) (kl : ι × ι) => M (ij.2, ij.1) (kl.2, kl.1)
    23	
    24	/-- `swapDensity` is equal to reindexing by the product-commutation equivalence. -/
    25	lemma swapDensity_eq_reindex {ι : Type*}
    26	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    27	    swapDensity X = Matrix.reindex (Equiv.prodComm ι ι) (Equiv.prodComm ι ι) X := by
    28	  ext x y
    29	  rcases x with ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
    30	  rcases y with ⟨j₁, j₂⟩
    31	  rfl
    32	
    33	@[simp] lemma swapDensity_swapDensity {ι : Type*}
    34	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    35	    swapDensity (swapDensity X) = X := by
    36	  ext x y
    37	  rcases x with ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
    38	  rcases y with ⟨j₁, j₂⟩
    39	  rfl

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Algebra.FieldBasis

     6	/-!
     7	# The low-degree game
     8	
     9	This file introduces the finite question and answer alphabets used by the
    10	low-degree component of the Pauli basis test.  The maps are explicit maps on
    11	the ambient coefficient space; their conditional-linearity and distribution
    12	invariants are recorded as proof-level obligations for later stages.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
    17	`def:ld-win-predicate` in
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`; their paper origin is
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient
    31	space uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a
    32	model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for
    33	`def:ld-game` in
    34	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    36	-/
    37	structure LdParams where
    38	  q : ℕ
    39	  m : ℕ
    40	  d : ℕ
    41	  k : ℕ
    42	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    43	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    44	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    45	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    46	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    47	
    48	/-- The positive dimension in `LdParams` supplies the finite coordinate type
    49	used by the uniform axis and prefix-index marginals. -/
    50	instance (L : LdParams) : Nonempty (Fin L.m) :=
    51	  ⟨⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm⟩⟩
    52	
    53	/-- The fixed model accessor for an `LdParams` record.  It is a compatibility
    54	view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently quantified
    55	parameter.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    56	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    57	-/
    58	noncomputable def LdParams.model (P : LdParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    59	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
    60	
    61	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    62	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, selected globally by `LdParams.model`.
    63	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    64	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    65	-/
    66	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := (P.model).K
    67	
    68	/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    69	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    70	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    71	-/
    72	inductive LdType where
    73	  | point
    74	  | aline
    75	  | dline
    76	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    77	
    78	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    79	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    80	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    81	-/
    82	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    83	
    84	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    85	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    87	-/
    88	abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P
    89	
    90	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    91	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    92	-/
    93	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    94	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    95	
    96	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    97	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    98	-/
    99	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
   100	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
   101	
   102	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
   103	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   104	-/
   105	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   106	  fun i => z (.inr i)
   107	
   108	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   109	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   110	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   111	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   112	-/
   113	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   114	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   115	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   116	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   117	
   118	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   119	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   120	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   121	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   122	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   123	-/
   124	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   125	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   126	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   127	
   128	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   129	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   130	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   131	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   132	-/
   133	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   134	  fun i => match i with
   135	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   136	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   137	  | .inr _ => 0
   138	
   139	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   140	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   141	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   142	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   143	-/
   144	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   145	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   146	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   147	  fun i => match i with
   148	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   149	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   150	  | .inr _ => 0
   151	
   152	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   153	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   154	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   155	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper origin
   156	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   157	-/
   158	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   159	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   160	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   161	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   162	  fun i => match i with
   163	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   164	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   165	  | .inr j => direction j
   166	
   167	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   168	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   169	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   170	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   171	-/
   172	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   173	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   174	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   175	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P
   176	
   177	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the affine-line map.  This is a named
   178	Lean proof obligation for the prose assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`,
   179	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper
   180	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   181	-/
   182	theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :
   183	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 2 (ldALineCL P) := by
   184	  sorry
   185	
   186	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the diagonal-line map.  This is the
   187	level-3 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   188	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   189	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   190	-/
   191	theorem isCondLinear_ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) :
   192	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 3 (ldDLineCL P) := by
   193	  sorry
   194	
   195	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
   196	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
   197	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   198	-/
   199	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
   200	
   201	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   202	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   203	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   204	-/
   205	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   206	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   207	  Distribution.map
   208	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   209	    (fun s =>
   210	      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   211	
   212	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   213	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   214	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   215	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`; paper
   216	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   217	-/
   218	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   219	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   220	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   221	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   222	  deriving DecidableEq
   223	
   224	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   225	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   226	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   227	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   228	-/
   229	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   230	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   231	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   232	      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
   233	
   234	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   235	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   236	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   237	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   238	-/
   239	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   240	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   241	  toFun
   242	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   243	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   244	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   245	  invFun
   246	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   247	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   248	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   249	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   250	  right_inv := by
   251	    intro x
   252	    cases x with
   253	    | inl a => rfl
   254	    | inr x =>
   255	        cases x with
   256	        | inl a => rfl
   257	        | inr a => rfl
   258	
   259	instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   260	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩
   261	
   262	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   263	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
   264	
   265	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   266	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   267	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   268	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   269	-/
   270	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   271	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   272	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   273	
   274	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   275	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   276	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   277	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   278	-/
   279	def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   280	  match t, a with
   281	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   282	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   283	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   284	  | _, _ => false
   285	
   286	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   287	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   288	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   289	-/
   290	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   291	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   292	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   293	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   294	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   295	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   296	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   297	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   298	
   299	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   300	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   301	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   302	-/
   303	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   304	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   305	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   306	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   307	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   308	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   309	
   310	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   311	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   312	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   313	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   314	-/
   315	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   316	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   317	  open Classical in
   318	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   319	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   320	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   321	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   322	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   323	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   324	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   325	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   326	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   327	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   328	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   329	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   330	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   331	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   332	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   333	      else false
   334	
   335	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   336	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   337	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   338	-/
   339	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   340	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   341	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   342	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   343	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   344	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   345	  μ_prob := by sorry
   346	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   347	
   348	end
   349	
   350	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.DiagonalLine
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# One-variable line polynomials for the low individual degree test
     5	
     6	Polynomial answer types attached to axis-parallel and diagonal lines.
     7	
     8	## References
     9	
    10	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex`
    11	- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch02_test.tex`
    12	-/
    13	
    14	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT
    15	
    16	/-- A coded function has low individual degree when it is represented by an actual
    17	multivariate polynomial over the chosen field model whose degree in each variable is at
    18	most `d`. -/
    19	def HasLowIndividualDegree (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    20	    (g : Point params → Fq params) : Prop :=
    21	  ∃ p : PolynomialModel params,
    22	    (∀ i, MvPolynomial.degreeOf i p ≤ params.d) ∧
    23	      g = evalPolynomialModel params p
    24	
    25	/-- A coded univariate function has degree at most `bound` when it is represented by
    26	an actual polynomial over the chosen field model of degree at most `bound`. -/
    27	def HasUnivariateDegreeAtMost (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    28	    (bound : ℕ) (f : Fq params → Fq params) : Prop :=
    29	  ∃ p : LinePolynomialModel params,
    30	    p.natDegree ≤ bound ∧
    31	      f = evalLinePolynomialModel params p
    32	
    33	/-- Composing with the degree-one translation `C a + X` preserves `natDegree`
    34	bounds.  Shared degree bookkeeping for the `reparamAt` reparametrizations
    35	below. -/
    36	theorem natDegree_comp_C_add_X_le {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    37	    (p : LinePolynomialModel params) (a : Scalar params) {n : ℕ}
    38	    (hp : p.natDegree ≤ n) :

    25	/-- The canonical affine parameterization `t ↦ base + t · direction`. -/
    26	def pointAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    27	    (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) : Fq params → Point params :=
    28	  fun t => addPoint ℓ.base (smulPoint t ℓ.direction)
    29	
    30	/-- The support of the nonzero coordinates of a direction vector. -/
    31	noncomputable def nonzeroDirectionSupport {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    32	    (v : Point params) : Finset (Fin params.m) :=
    33	  Finset.univ.filter fun i => v i ≠ zeroCoord
    34	
    35	/-- The least nonzero coordinate of a direction vector, when one exists. -/
    36	noncomputable def firstNonzeroCoord? {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    37	    (v : Point params) : Option (Fin params.m) :=
    38	  open Classical in
    39	  let s := nonzeroDirectionSupport (params := params) v
    40	  if hs : s.Nonempty then some (s.min' hs) else none
    41	
    42	/-- Normalize a direction vector so its first nonzero coordinate becomes `1`. -/
    43	noncomputable def normalizeDirection {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    44	    (v : Point params) : Point params :=
    45	  open Classical in
    46	  match firstNonzeroCoord? (params := params) v with
    47	    | none => zeroPoint
    48	    | some i => smulPoint (invCoord (v i)) v
    49	
    50	/-- Canonical geometric diagonal line through `u` in direction `v`.
    51	
    52	For nonzero `v`, we normalize by the first nonzero coordinate and shift the
    53	base point so that this pivot coordinate is `0`. The degenerate `v = 0` case is
    54	kept as the singleton line through `u`. -/
    55	noncomputable def throughPointDirection {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    56	    (u v : Point params) : DiagonalLine params :=
    57	  open Classical in
    58	  match firstNonzeroCoord? (params := params) v with
    59	    | none => { base := u, direction := zeroPoint }
    60	    | some i =>
    61	        let w := normalizeDirection (params := params) v
    62	        let t := u i
    63	        { base := fun j => subCoord (u j) (mulCoord t (w j))
    64	          direction := w }

    66	/-- Affine parameter of the sampled point on the canonical diagonal line through
    67	`u` in direction `v`. -/
    68	noncomputable def sampleParameter {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    69	    (u v : Point params) : Fq params :=
    70	  open Classical in
    71	  match firstNonzeroCoord? (params := params) v with
    72	    | none => zeroCoord
    73	    | some i => u i

    79	  funext j
    80	  by_cases h : j = i
    81	  · subst h
    82	    unfold AxisParallelLine.pointAt AxisParallelLine.throughPoint
    83	    simp [AxisParallelLine.sampleParameter, addCoord, zeroCoord]
    84	  · simp [AxisParallelLine.throughPoint, AxisParallelLine.pointAt, h]

    89	        (DiagonalLine.sampleParameter (params := params) u v) = u := by
    90	  classical

    92	  split
    93	  · funext j
    94	    simp [DiagonalLine.pointAt, addPoint, smulPoint, zeroPoint,

   142	             (rebaseAt
   143	               ({ base := base, direction := direction } : DiagonalLine params) t).pointAt s,
   144	           direction := direction } : DiagonalLine params) =
   145	        ({ base :=
   146	             ({ base := base, direction := direction } : DiagonalLine params).pointAt
   147	               (addCoord t s),
   148	           direction := direction } : DiagonalLine params)

   153	/-- Embed a diagonal line into the slice at height `x`, keeping the new coordinate fixed. -/
   154	def appendAtHeight (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
   155	    (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) (x : Fq params) : DiagonalLine params.next where
   156	  base := appendPoint params ℓ.base x
   157	  direction := appendPoint params ℓ.direction zeroCoord

   159	@[simp] theorem appendAtHeight_rebaseAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   160	    (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) (t x : Fq params) :
   161	    appendAtHeight params (rebaseAt ℓ t) x =
   162	      rebaseAt (appendAtHeight params ℓ x) t := by
   163	  cases ℓ with
   164	  | mk base direction =>
   165	      change
   166	        ({ base := appendPoint params (addPoint base (smulPoint t direction)) x,
   167	           direction := appendPoint params direction zeroCoord } : DiagonalLine params.next) =
   168	        ({ base := addPoint (appendPoint params base x)
   169	             (smulPoint t (appendPoint params direction zeroCoord)),
   170	           direction := appendPoint params direction zeroCoord } : DiagonalLine params.next)
   171	      congr
   172	      funext i
   173	      by_cases hi : i.1 < params.m
   174	      · simp only [appendPoint, addPoint, smulPoint, addCoord, mulCoord, hi, ↓reduceDIte]
   175	        rfl
   176	      · simp only [appendPoint, hi, ↓reduceDIte, addPoint, addCoord, smulPoint, mulCoord,
   177	          zeroCoord, decode_encodeScalar]
   178	        rw [← encode_decodeScalar x]
   179	        congr 1
   180	        calc
   181	          decodeScalar x = decodeScalar x + decodeScalar t * (0 : Scalar params) := by ring
   182	          _ = decodeScalar (encodeScalar (decodeScalar x)) +
   183	                decodeScalar t * decodeScalar (encodeScalar 0) := by
   184	              rw [show decodeScalar (encodeScalar (decodeScalar x)) = decodeScalar x from
   185	                  decode_encodeScalar (decodeScalar x),
   186	                show decodeScalar (encodeScalar (0 : Scalar params)) = (0 : Scalar params) from
   187	                  decode_encodeScalar (0 : Scalar params)]

   761	/-- Paper-faithful two-space projective strategy data.
   762	
   763	This matches the paper's `def:general-projective-strategy`
   764	(`test_definition.tex`, lines 98--115): Alice's and Bob's measurements act on
   765	separate local carriers `ιA` and `ιB`, and the bipartite state lives on
   766	`ιA × ιB` without a built-in swap symmetry.
   767	
   768	The `isNormalized` field records that the bipartite state's density operator
   769	has normalized trace `1`.
   770	
   771	The four covariance conditions express that the line-indexed projectors
   772	descend from chosen affine parametrizations to geometric lines; transport and
   773	zero-coordinate evaluation are equivalent consequences. -/
   774	structure ProjStrat (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
   775	    (ιA : Type*) [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
   776	    (ιB : Type*) [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] where
   777	  /-- Bipartite state on the tensor product of Alice's and Bob's local carriers. -/
   778	  state : QuantumState (ιA × ιB)
   779	  /-- The bipartite state's density operator is trace-normalized. -/

80	A \emph{symmetric, projective strategy} for the $(m,q, d)$-low individual degree test
    81	is a tuple $(\psi, A, B, L)$ defined as follows.
    82	\begin{itemize}
    83	\item[$\circ$] $\ket{\psi} \in \calH \ot \calH$ is a bipartite, permutation-invariant state.
    84	\item[$\circ$] $A = \{A^u_a\}$ contains a matrix for each $u \in \F_q^m$ and $a \in \F_q$.
    85				For each $u$, $A^u$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH$.
    86	\item[$\circ$] $B = \{B^{\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each axis-parallel line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
    87				and univariate degree-$d$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
    88				For each $\ell$, $B^{\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH$.
    89	\item[$\circ$] $L = \{L^{\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
    90				and univariate degree-$md$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
    91				For each $\ell$, $L^{\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH$.
    92	\end{itemize}
    93	\end{definition}
    94	
    95	We can also consider more general strategies which are no longer assumed to be symmetric.
    96	In this case, Players~$\mathrm{A}$ and~$\mathrm{B}$ each have their own versions of the measurements~$A$, $B$, and~$L$.
    97	
    98	\begin{definition}[General projective strategy]
    99	A \emph{projective strategy} for the $(m,q, d)$-low individual degree test
   100	is a tuple $(\psi, A^{\mathrm{A}},B^{\mathrm{A}},L^{\mathrm{A}},A^{\mathrm{B}},B^{\mathrm{B}},L^{\mathrm{B}})$ defined as follows.
   101	\begin{itemize}
   102	\item[$\circ$] $\ket{\psi} \in \calH_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}}$ is a bipartite state.
   103	\end{itemize}
   104	Furthermore, for each~$w \in \{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}\}$:
   105	\begin{itemize}
   106	\item[$\circ$] $A^{w} = \{A^{w,u}_a\}$ contains a matrix for each $u \in \F_q^m$ and $a \in \F_q$.
   107				For each $u$, $A^{w,u}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.
   108	\item[$\circ$] $B^{w} = \{B^{w,\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each axis-parallel line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
   109				and univariate degree-$d$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
   110				For each $\ell$, $B^{w,\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.
   111	\item[$\circ$] $L^w = \{L^{w,\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
   112				and univariate degree-$md$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
   113				For each $\ell$, $L^{w,\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.
   114	\end{itemize}
   115	\end{definition}
   116	
   117	\begin{remark}
   118	Throughout this work, we will only consider projective strategies.
   119	So we will henceforth use the terms ``strategy" and ``symmetric strategy'' to refer exclusively to projective strategies and symmetric, projective strategies, respectively.
   120	
   121	In addition, we will spend the vast majority of this work dealing solely with symmetric strategies, as they are notationally simpler to work with.
   122	Much of this work will focus on proving~\Cref{thm:main-induction},
   123	a variant of our main theorem for symmetric strategies.
   124	Our main theorem for general strategies, \Cref{thm:main-formal} below, will be proven in \Cref{sec:induction} by a standard reduction to the symmetric case.
   125	We will only see these more cumbersome-to-write general strategies
   126	in this section, where we state \Cref{thm:main-formal},
   127	and in \Cref{sec:induction}, where we carry out the reduction.
   128	\end{remark}
   129	
   130	\begin{definition}[Good strategy]
   131	A strategy is $(\eps, \delta, \gamma)$-good if it
   132	passes the axis-parallel lines test with probability at least $1-\eps$,
   133	the self consistency test with probability at least~$1-\delta$,
   134	and the diagonal lines test with probability at least~$1-\gamma$.
   135	\end{definition}
   136	
   137	\begin{remark}\label{rem:good-strat-characterization}
   138	Using notation which will be introduced in \Cref{sec:comparing-measurements} below,
   139	a symmetric strategy is $(\eps, \delta, \gamma)$-good
   140	if and only if it satisfies the following three conditions.
   141	For $\bell$ and $\bu$ as in the axis-parallel lines test,
   142	\begin{equation*}
   143	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\eps} I \ot B^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]},
   144	\quad
   145	\text{and}
   146	\quad
   147	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot A^u_a.
   148	\end{equation*}
   149	And for $\bell$ and $\bu$ as in the diagonal lines test,
   150	\begin{equation*}
   151	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\gamma} I \ot L^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]}.
   152	\end{equation*}
   153	\end{remark}
   154	
   155	\begin{notation}\label{not:conditioned-on-last-direction}
   156	Our proof will be via induction,
   157	i.e.\ proving soundness of the $(m+1,q,d)$-low individual degree test
   158	using the soundness of the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.
   159	To do this, we will frequently use the axis-parallel line test in the specific case of $i = m+1$.
   160	Thus, it will be convenient to introduce the following notation.
   161	Let $(\psi, A, B, L)$ be a symmetric strategy for the $(m+1, q, d)$-low individual degree test,
   162	Then for each $u \in \F_q^m$ we will write $B^u_f$ as shorthand for $B^{\ell}_f$,
   163	where $\ell = \{(u, x) \mid x \in \F_q\}$.
   164	For a function $f:\ell \rightarrow \F_q$,
   165	we will also sometimes write $f(x)$ as shorthand for $f(u,x)$.
   166	\end{notation}
   167	
   168	\begin{definition}
   169	Consider the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.
   170	For $j \in \{1, \ldots, m\}$,
   171	we refer to the \emph{$j$-restricted diagonal lines test}
   172	as the diagonal lines test conditioned on $\bi = j$.
   173	For example, in the $m$-restricted diagonal lines test,
   174	the line $\bell$ is simply a uniformly random line in $\F_q^m$.
   175	\end{definition}
   176	
   177	Now we state our main theorem using notation which will be introduced in \Cref{sec:prelims} below.
   178	This the formal version of \Cref{thm:main-informal}.
   179	
   180	\begin{theorem}[Main theorem; quantum soundness of the low individual degree test]\label{thm:main-formal}
   181	  Consider a projective strategy $(\psi, A^{\mathrm{A}},B^{\mathrm{A}},L^{\mathrm{A}},A^{\mathrm{B}},B^{\mathrm{B}},L^{\mathrm{B}})$ 
   182	   which passes the  $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test with probability at least $1-\eps$.
   183	  Let $k \geq md$ be an integer.
   184	  Let
   185	  \begin{equation*}
   186	  \nu = 100000 k^2m^4 \cdot \Big(\eps^{1/40000} + (d/q)^{1/40000} + e^{-k/(2560000m^2)}\Big).
   187	  \end{equation*}
   188	Then there exists projective measurements $G^{\mathrm{A}}, G^{\mathrm{B}} \in \polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ with the following properties:
   189	\begin{enumerate}
   190	  \item (Consistency with~$A$):  On average over $\bu \sim \F_q^{m}$,
   191		  \begin{align*}
   192		  A^{\mathrm{A},u}_a \otimes I
   193		  	&\simeq_{\nu} I \otimes G^{\mathrm{B}}_{[g(u)=a]},\\
   194		I \otimes A^{\mathrm{B},u}_a
   195		  	&\simeq_{\nu}  G^{\mathrm{A}}_{[g(u)=a]} \ot I.
   196		  \end{align*}
   197	\item (Self-consistency):
   198		\begin{equation*}
   199		G^{\mathrm{A}}_g \ot I \simeq_{\nu} I \ot G^{\mathrm{B}}_g.
   200		\end{equation*}
   201	\end{enumerate}
   202	\end{theorem}
   203	
   204	We note that there is a tradeoff in \Cref{thm:main-formal} specified by the parameter~$k$.
   205	As~$k$ increases, $\nu$'s prefactor $k^2$ increases.
   206	On the other hand, as $k$ increases, the term $e^{- k/(2560000m^2)}$ which also occurs in $\nu$ \emph{decreases}.
   207	Thus, when applying this theorem, one must select~$k$ to balance these competing demands.
   208	Typically, choosing $k = \poly(m)$ should be more than sufficient for applications.
   209	We believe that this parameter~$k$ is an artifact of our proof,
   210	and we hope that it will be removed in the future.
   211

     3	/-!
     4	# Strategy transport for the directly indexed low-degree game
     5	
     6	This module reads one coordinate of a projective directly indexed strategy as
     7	a two-space mature low individual degree strategy.  Canonical line
     8	representatives and answer reparametrization establish all four covariance
     9	conditions.  It also records exact Born-weight formulas for both directions
    10	of strategy transport.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-458`
    15	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:98-151`
    16	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	/-! ## Canonical line rebasing for the mature LDT interface -/
    29	
    30	/-- A point differs from its canonical representative by a scalar multiple of
    31	the line direction. -/
    32	theorem mem_linePoints_direct_lineRepMap
    33	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} (v u : Fin m → K) :
    34	    u ∈ linePoints (lineRepMap v u) v := by
    35	  let W : Submodule K (Fin m → K) := Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))
    36	  let T : Submodule K (Fin m → K) :=
    37	    registerSubmodule K (canonicalComplement W)
    38	  have hdiff : u - lineRepMap v u ∈ W := by
    39	    simpa [lineRepMap, canonicalProjOfKernel, W, T, LinearMap.comp_apply] using
    40	      (Submodule.sub_projection_mem
    41	        (isCompl_registerSubmodule_canonicalComplement W).symm u)
    42	  rcases Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mp hdiff with ⟨t, ht⟩
    43	  refine ⟨t, ?_⟩
    44	  rw [ht]
    45	  abel

    47	/-- A chosen affine parameter expressing a point relative to its canonical
    48	line representative. -/
    49	noncomputable def directLineRepParameter
    50	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} (v u : Fin m → K) : K :=
    51	  Classical.choose (mem_linePoints_direct_lineRepMap v u)
    52	
    53	/-- The chosen canonical rebase parameter reconstructs the original point. -/
    54	theorem directLineRepParameter_spec
    55	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} (v u : Fin m → K) :
    56	    u = lineRepMap v u + directLineRepParameter v u • v :=
    57	  Classical.choose_spec (mem_linePoints_direct_lineRepMap v u)
    58	
    59	/-- Canonical line representatives are unchanged by translation along their
    60	direction. -/
    61	theorem lineRepMap_add_smul
    62	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    63	    (v u : Fin m → K) (t : K) :
    64	    lineRepMap v (u + t • v) = lineRepMap v u := by
    65	  let W : Submodule K (Fin m → K) := Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))
    66	  have hv : v ∈ W := Submodule.subset_span (Set.mem_singleton v)
    67	  have hzero : lineRepMap v v = 0 := by
    68	    simp [lineRepMap, canonicalProjOfKernel, W, LinearMap.comp_apply,
    69	      Submodule.projectionOnto_apply_of_mem_right
    70	        (isCompl_registerSubmodule_canonicalComplement W).symm hv]
    71	  simp [map_add, map_smul, hzero]
    72	
    73	/-- For a nonzero direction, the canonical rebase parameter is unique. -/
    74	theorem directLineRepParameter_eq_of_nonzero
    75	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    76	    {v u : Fin m → K} (hv : v ≠ 0) {t : K}
    77	    (ht : u = lineRepMap v u + t • v) :
    78	    directLineRepParameter v u = t := by
    79	  have hfun : directLineRepParameter v u • v = t • v := by
    80	    apply add_left_cancel (a := lineRepMap v u)
    81	    exact (directLineRepParameter_spec v u).symm.trans ht
    82	  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ : ∃ i, v i ≠ 0 := by
    83	    by_contra h
    84	    apply hv
    85	    funext i
    86	    simpa using not_exists.mp h i
    87	  have hcoord := congrFun hfun i
    88	  simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul] at hcoord
    89	  exact mul_right_cancel₀ hi hcoord
    90	
    91	/-- Translating a point on a nonzero line adds the translation to its
    92	canonical rebase parameter. -/
    93	theorem directLineRepParameter_add_smul
    94	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    95	    {v u : Fin m → K} (hv : v ≠ 0) (t : K) :
    96	    directLineRepParameter v (u + t • v) =
    97	      directLineRepParameter v u + t := by
    98	  apply directLineRepParameter_eq_of_nonzero hv
    99	  rw [lineRepMap_add_smul]
   100	  calc
   101	    u + t • v =
   102	        (lineRepMap v u + directLineRepParameter v u • v) + t • v := by
   103	      rw [← directLineRepParameter_spec v u]
   104	    _ = lineRepMap v u + (directLineRepParameter v u + t) • v := by
   105	      module

   107	/-- Decode a mature LDT point into the fixed direct scalar field. -/
   108	abbrev ldtPointToDirect (D : DirectLdParams) :
   109	    Point D.toLDTParameters → Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   110	  (directPointEquiv D).symm

   112	/-- The direct canonical axis question represented by a mature axis line. -/
   113	noncomputable def directAxisQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   114	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   115	  let u := ldtPointToDirect D line.base
   116	  let v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D := coordinateDirection line.direction
   117	  (.aline, ⟨lineRepMap v u, line.direction, 0⟩)
   118	
   119	/-- The direct canonical diagonal question represented by a mature diagonal
   120	line.  The first direct index is valid for every direction. -/
   121	noncomputable def directDiagonalQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   122	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   123	  let u := ldtPointToDirect D line.base
   124	  let v := ldtPointToDirect D line.direction
   125	  (.dline, ⟨lineRepMap v u, D.firstIndex, v⟩)
   126	
   127	/-- The direct point question represented by a mature LDT point. -/
   128	noncomputable def directPointQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   129	    (u : Point D.toLDTParameters) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   130	  directLdPointQuestionOf D (ldtPointToDirect D u)

   132	/-- Decoding an axis-line rebase is translation by the decoded scalar along
   133	the corresponding direct coordinate direction. -/
   134	theorem ldtPointToDirect_axis_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   135	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters)
   136	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   137	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   138	    ldtPointToDirect D (line.rebaseAt t).base =
   139	      ldtPointToDirect D line.base +
   140	        (directScalarEquiv D).symm t •
   141	          coordinateDirection line.direction := by
   142	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   143	  funext i
   144	  simp only [ldtPointToDirect, directPointEquiv_symm_apply,
   145	    AxisParallelLine.rebaseAt, AxisParallelLine.pointAt, Pi.add_apply,
   146	    Pi.smul_apply]
   147	  by_cases hi : i = line.direction
   148	  · subst i
   149	    simp only [coordinateDirection, if_pos, smul_eq_mul]
   150	    rw [Pi.single_eq_same, mul_one]
   151	    exact (FieldModel.equiv (q := D.q)).symm_apply_apply _
   152	  · simp [hi, coordinateDirection]
   153	
   154	/-- Decoding a diagonal-line rebase is translation by the decoded scalar
   155	along the decoded direct direction. -/
   156	theorem ldtPointToDirect_diagonal_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   157	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters)
   158	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   159	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   160	    ldtPointToDirect D (line.rebaseAt t).base =
   161	      ldtPointToDirect D line.base +
   162	        (directScalarEquiv D).symm t • ldtPointToDirect D line.direction := by
   163	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   164	  funext i
   165	  change decodeScalar
   166	      (addCoord (line.base i) (mulCoord t (line.direction i))) =
   167	    decodeScalar (line.base i) + decodeScalar t * decodeScalar (line.direction i)
   168	  simp [addCoord, mulCoord]

   170	/-- Canonical direct axis questions do not depend on the chosen base point of
   171	the mature line. -/
   172	theorem directAxisQuestionOf_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   173	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters)
   174	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   175	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   176	    directAxisQuestionOf D (line.rebaseAt t) = directAxisQuestionOf D line := by
   177	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   178	  simp only [directAxisQuestionOf, AxisParallelLine.rebaseAt_direction]
   179	  rw [ldtPointToDirect_axis_rebase, lineRepMap_add_smul]
   180	
   181	/-- Canonical direct diagonal questions do not depend on the chosen base point
   182	of the mature line. -/
   183	theorem directDiagonalQuestionOf_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   184	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters)
   185	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   186	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   187	    directDiagonalQuestionOf D (line.rebaseAt t) =
   188	      directDiagonalQuestionOf D line := by
   189	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   190	  simp only [directDiagonalQuestionOf, DiagonalLine.rebaseAt]
   191	  have hrebase := ldtPointToDirect_diagonal_rebase D line t
   192	  change ldtPointToDirect D (line.pointAt t) =
   193	      ldtPointToDirect D line.base +
   194	        (directScalarEquiv D).symm t • ldtPointToDirect D line.direction at hrebase
   195	  rw [hrebase, lineRepMap_add_smul]

   197	/-- The fixed scalar coding transports field addition to mature coordinate
   198	addition. -/
   199	theorem directScalarEquiv_add (D : DirectLdParams)
   200	    (x y : DirectScalarQ D) :
   201	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   202	    directScalarEquiv D (x + y) =
   203	      addCoord (directScalarEquiv D x) (directScalarEquiv D y) := by
   204	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   205	  change FieldModel.equiv (x + y) =
   206	    FieldModel.equiv
   207	      (FieldModel.equiv.symm (FieldModel.equiv x) +
   208	        FieldModel.equiv.symm (FieldModel.equiv y))
   209	  rw [FieldModel.equiv.symm_apply_apply, FieldModel.equiv.symm_apply_apply]

   215	  have hi := congrFun h i
   216	  simp [coordinateDirection] at hi

   230	/-- Axis-line canonical parameters add under mature rebasing. -/
   231	theorem directAxisRebaseParameter_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   232	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters)
   233	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   234	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   235	    directAxisRebaseParameter D (line.rebaseAt t) =
   236	      directAxisRebaseParameter D line + (directScalarEquiv D).symm t := by
   237	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   238	  unfold directAxisRebaseParameter
   239	  rw [ldtPointToDirect_axis_rebase]
   240	  exact directLineRepParameter_add_smul
   241	    (coordinateDirection_ne_zero line.direction) _

   243	/-- Nonzero diagonal-line canonical parameters add under mature rebasing. -/
   244	theorem directDiagonalRebaseParameter_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   245	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters)
   246	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters)
   247	    (hdir : ldtPointToDirect D line.direction ≠ 0) :
   248	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel

   250	      directDiagonalRebaseParameter D line + (directScalarEquiv D).symm t := by
   251	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   252	  unfold directDiagonalRebaseParameter
   253	  rw [ldtPointToDirect_diagonal_rebase]
   254	  exact directLineRepParameter_add_smul hdir _

   256	/-- Read one simultaneous coordinate from a direct point answer. -/
   257	noncomputable def directPointAnswerReadout (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k) :
   258	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   259	    DirectLdAnswer D → Fq D.toLDTParameters := by
   260	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   261	  intro answer
   262	  exact match answer with
   263	    | .pointVals a => directScalarEquiv D (a r)
   264	    | .alinePolys _ => directScalarEquiv D 0
   265	    | .dlinePolys _ => directScalarEquiv D 0

   267	/-- Read one simultaneous coordinate from a direct axis-line answer and
   268	rebase its polynomial from the canonical direct line to the mature line. -/
   269	noncomputable def directAxisAnswerReadout (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
   270	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters) :
   271	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   272	    DirectLdAnswer D → AxisLinePolynomial D.toLDTParameters := by
   273	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   274	  intro answer
   275	  exact match answer with
   276	    | .alinePolys a => AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAt
   277	        (directAxisAnswerEquiv D (a r))
   278	        (directScalarEquiv D (directAxisRebaseParameter D line))
   279	    | .pointVals _ => default
   280	    | .dlinePolys _ => default

   282	/-- Read one simultaneous coordinate from a direct diagonal-line answer.  A
   283	zero direction is a singleton geometric line, so it is sent to the
   284	translation-fixed default polynomial; nonzero directions use canonical
   285	rebasing. -/
   286	noncomputable def directDiagonalAnswerReadout (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
   287	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters) :
   288	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   289	    DirectLdAnswer D → DiagonalLinePolynomial D.toLDTParameters := by
   290	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   291	  intro answer
   292	  by_cases hdir : ldtPointToDirect D line.direction = 0
   293	  · exact default
   294	  · exact match answer with
   295	    | .dlinePolys a => DiagonalLinePolynomial.reparamAt
   296	        (directDiagonalAnswerEquiv D (a r))
   297	        (directScalarEquiv D (directDiagonalRebaseParameter D line))
   298	    | .pointVals _ => default
   299	    | .alinePolys _ => default

   301	/-- Axis answer readout is covariant under mature line rebasing. -/
   302	theorem directAxisAnswerReadout_rebase (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
   303	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters)
   304	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) :
   305	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   306	    directAxisAnswerReadout D r (line.rebaseAt t) answer =
   307	      AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAt (directAxisAnswerReadout D r line answer) t := by
   308	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   309	  cases answer with
   310	  | pointVals a => simp [directAxisAnswerReadout]
   311	  | dlinePolys a => simp [directAxisAnswerReadout]
   312	  | alinePolys a =>
   313	      simp only [directAxisAnswerReadout]
   314	      rw [directAxisRebaseParameter_rebase, directScalarEquiv_add]
   315	      rw [(directScalarEquiv D).apply_symm_apply]
   316	      exact (AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAt_reparamAt
   317	        (directAxisAnswerEquiv D (a r)) _ _).symm
   318	
   319	/-- Diagonal answer readout is covariant under mature line rebasing, including
   320	the singleton zero-direction convention. -/
   321	theorem directDiagonalAnswerReadout_rebase (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
   322	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters)
   323	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) :
   324	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   325	    directDiagonalAnswerReadout D r (line.rebaseAt t) answer =
   326	      DiagonalLinePolynomial.reparamAt
   327	        (directDiagonalAnswerReadout D r line answer) t := by
   328	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   329	  by_cases hdir : ldtPointToDirect D line.direction = 0
   330	  · have hrebase : ldtPointToDirect D (line.rebaseAt t).direction = 0 := by
   331	      simpa [DiagonalLine.rebaseAt] using hdir
   332	    simp [directDiagonalAnswerReadout, hdir, hrebase]
   333	  · have hrebase : ldtPointToDirect D (line.rebaseAt t).direction ≠ 0 := by
   334	      simpa [DiagonalLine.rebaseAt] using hdir
   335	    cases answer with
   336	    | pointVals a =>
   337	        simp [directDiagonalAnswerReadout, hdir, hrebase]
   338	    | alinePolys a =>
   339	        simp [directDiagonalAnswerReadout, hdir, hrebase]
   340	    | dlinePolys a =>
   341	        simp only [directDiagonalAnswerReadout, hdir, hrebase, dite_false]
   342	        rw [directDiagonalRebaseParameter_rebase D line t hdir,
   343	          directScalarEquiv_add, (directScalarEquiv D).apply_symm_apply]
   344	        exact (DiagonalLinePolynomial.reparamAt_reparamAt
   345	          (directDiagonalAnswerEquiv D (a r)) _ _).symm

    24	/-- Evaluation after adjoining an unused coordinate agrees with evaluation before

    40	/-- View a global polynomial submeasurement as a point-indexed answer family. -/

    42	    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]

    44	    IdxSubMeas (Point params) (Fq params) ι :=

    47	/-- View a global polynomial measurement as a point-indexed answer measurement family.
    48	
    49	The submeasurement-valued `polynomialEvaluationFamily` is the form used by most
    50	consistency statements.  The heterogeneous triangle step in the final theorem
    51	uses complete measurements, so this version keeps the same postprocessing while
    52	retaining the total-mass proof. -/
    53	noncomputable def polynomialEvaluationMeasurementFamily
    54	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    55	    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    56	    (G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι) :
    57	    IdxMeas (Point params) (Fq params) ι :=

   688	/-- Correlated residue registers turn two block-diagonal effects into the
   689	uniform average of their matching source-block Born weights. -/
   690	private theorem seedFiberBlockBornAmplitude
   691	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams)
   692	    (A : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιA)
   693	    (B : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιB) :
   694	    vectorBornAmplitude (seedFiberLiftedState S L)
   695	        (Matrix.blockDiagonal A) (Matrix.blockDiagonal B) =
   696	      (Fintype.card (Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
   697	        ∑ residue, vectorBornAmplitude S.ψ (A residue) (B residue) := by
   698	  classical
   699	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   700	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   701	  unfold vectorBornAmplitude applyOperatorToState heteroKron Matrix.kronecker
   702	  simp_rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
   703	  simp only [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_apply,
   704	    dotProduct, Matrix.mulVec]
   705	  simp_rw [← Finset.univ_product_univ, Finset.sum_product]
   706	  simp [seedFiberLiftedState_apply, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply,
   707	    mul_assoc, mul_comm]

   709	  simp_rw [mul_assoc, ← Finset.mul_sum]
   710	  ring_nf

   720	/-- Correlated residue registers give the uniform average of the source-block
   721	Born weights. -/
   722	private theorem seedFiberBlockBornWeight
   723	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams)
   724	    (A : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιA)
   725	    (B : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιB) :
   726	    vectorBornWeight (seedFiberLiftedState S L)
   727	        (Matrix.blockDiagonal A) (Matrix.blockDiagonal B) =
   728	      (Fintype.card (Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
   729	        ∑ residue, vectorBornWeight S.ψ (A residue) (B residue) := by

   734	/-- The Born weight of the seed-bearing direct adapter is the uniform average

   736	theorem ldStrategyToDirect_bornWeight
   737	    (L : LdParams) (S : Strategy (ldGame L))
   738	    (x y : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   739	    (a b : DirectLdAnswer L.toDirectLdParams) :
   740	    strategyBornWeight (ldStrategyToDirect L S) x y a b =
   741	      (Fintype.card (Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
   742	        ∑ residue,
   743	          strategyBornWeight S
   744	            (seededLdQuestion L x residue)
   745	            (seededLdQuestion L y residue)
   746	            ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm a)
   747	            ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm b) := by

   749	      (Matrix.blockDiagonal fun residue =>
   750	        (S.A (seededLdQuestion L x residue)).effect
   751	          ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm a))
   752	      (Matrix.blockDiagonal fun residue =>
   753	        (S.B (seededLdQuestion L y residue)).effect
   754	          ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm b)) = _
   755	  exact seedFiberBlockBornWeight S L _ _

   757	/-- Read coordinate `r` of a projective direct-game strategy as a two-space
   758	projective strategy for the mature low individual degree interface. -/
   759	noncomputable def directCoordinateProjStrat
   760	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   761	    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
   762	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel

   776	    axisParallelMeasurementB := directCoordinateAxisMeasurement D r S.B hS.2

   784	/-- Point Born weights of the coordinate strategy are exactly the sums over
   785	the corresponding direct-answer readout fibers. -/
   786	theorem directCoordinateProjStrat_point_bornWeight
   787	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   788	    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k)
   789	    (u v : Point D.toLDTParameters)
   790	    (a b : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   791	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   792	    ev (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).state
   793	        (opTensor
   794	          (((directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementA u).outcome a)
   795	          (((directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementB v).outcome b)) =
   796	      ∑ directA ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   797	          directPointAnswerReadout D r answer = a),
   798	        ∑ directB ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   799	            directPointAnswerReadout D r answer = b),
   800	          strategyBornWeight S (directPointQuestionOf D u)
   801	            (directPointQuestionOf D v) directA directB := by
   802	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   803	  change ev (strategyQuantumState S)
   804	      (opTensor
   805	        ((ProjMeas.postprocess
   806	          (matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas
   807	            (S.A (directPointQuestionOf D u))
   808	            (hS.1 (directPointQuestionOf D u)))
   809	          (directPointAnswerReadout D r)).outcome a)

   813	            (hS.2 (directPointQuestionOf D v)))
   814	          (directPointAnswerReadout D r)).outcome b)) = _

   816	    (directPointQuestionOf D u) (directPointQuestionOf D v)
   817	    (directPointAnswerReadout D r) (directPointAnswerReadout D r) a b
   818	
   819	/-- Axis-line Born weights of the coordinate strategy are exactly the sums
   820	over the corresponding rebased direct-answer fibers. -/

   822	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   823	    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
   824	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel

   826	      (f g : AxisLinePolynomial D.toLDTParameters),

   845	          (matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas
